checks.check: Searching insrc connections exposes Manage Connections; command links and palette actions open same retained manager state.
checks.evidence: vscode-plugin/package.json:171 markdownDescription contains 'For insrc connections, [Manage Connections](command:insrc.openDataSources) opens the Saved and Temporary connection manager.' The same command id 'insrc.openDataSources' is registered via registerConnectionCommands(..., connectionManager) in extension.ts:339-340, routing both the palette command and the markdown link to the single ConnectionsManagerHost instance (host.open()), which reveals the existing panel if already open (host.ts:93-94: 'if(this.#panel){this.#panel.reveal();return;}').

checks.check: No/multiple registered roots explicit, actual workbench selected; command args only selection hints validated against fresh daemon state.
checks.evidence: wiring.ts ignores all command arguments (register(id, () => host.open())) and host.open() always re-fetches registeredRoots() from the daemon on each open (host.ts:107). The test (entry.test.ts:28-47) opens with zero registered roots (listState 'no-repository', roots []), then with two roots, and confirms every CONNECTION_COMMAND invoked with forged args ({repoRoot:'/unregistered', ...}) cannot change the draft or selected root, and registeredRoots is freshly read each open (reads===2).

checks.check: Only extension.ts imports vscode; dedicated connections types instead of unrelated panels/types.ts; preserve live registered command IDs.
checks.evidence: Grep for "from 'vscode'" under vscode-plugin/src/connections found no matches — host.ts, wiring.ts, types.ts, renderer.ts, etc. are vscode-free. types.ts (vscode-plugin/src/connections/types.ts) defines its own ConnectionIntent/ConnectionRenderView/ConnectionPanel rather than reusing panels/types.ts. Command ids ('insrc.openDataSources', 'insrc.connections.add/edit/test/remove') are identical across package.json, wiring.ts, packaging.test.ts and truthful-sync.test.ts — no renaming.

verdict.reason:
Manifest commands/configuration, extension.ts activation wiring, and the dedicated connections/wiring.ts module all match the Task's stated surface; the required integration test genuinely exercises manifest discovery, command-id uniqueness, palette/editor route equivalence, and fresh-daemon-state validation against forged args, and the daemon's typecheck and test runs both passed.</reason>
</invoke>
